text: dsh-backdoor-guard 是面向 DSH 的工具调用判定插件，通过 Cordis 插件钩子在工具分派前评估模型请求的操作。它收集最近的用户请求、工具名称、规范化参数、前置说明字符数和同轮先前调用，并把这些信息交给 systemone 兼容的判定端点。判定概率达到阈值时放行，低于阈值时拒绝调用并向会话注入提示。可配置模型、端点、阈值、超时、跳过的工具模式和判定失败时的处理方式。托管 Jev 可使用 TYPESAFE_API_KEY，也可配置本地判定服务。

dsh-backdoor-guard checks tool calls before dispatch. A judge evaluates call context; calls meeting the threshold proceed, while lower scores are denied. Configure the model, endpoint, threshold, timeout, skipped tools, and error behavior. Hosted Jev or a local judge can be used.
想在 DSH 分派工具操作前先让独立判定服务评估一下。
能不能根据用户请求和工具参数判断一次调用是否应该放行？
I want a judgment step before my DSH agent executes a tool call.
dsh-backdoor-guard 的功能「工具调用前判定」：在工具分派前向判定端点提交请求上下文、工具名称和参数；概率达到阈值则继续执行，低于阈值则拒绝并注入会话提示。
dsh-backdoor-guard 的功能「可配置判定策略」：管理员可设置概率阈值、超时、跳过的工具名称模式，以及判定服务出错时放行或拒绝的行为。
dsh-backdoor-guard 使用前须知：托管判定端点会接收最近的用户请求文本、工具名和参数；默认服务为 api.typesafe.ai，且可配置截断上限。

dsh-backdoor-guard README · dsh-backdoor-guard：English | [日本語](#日本語)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin that stops **trained-in backdoor payloads** — model weights (e.g. a malicious QLoRa merge) that fire a specific tool call or credential exfiltration when a hidden trigger appears — **before the tool executes**.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · dsh-backdoor-guard：Every model-requested tool call is priced by a dedicated **decision model** ([Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) hosted, or a self-hosted [LiquidAI d1](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B) via the bundled shim — both speak the same Decision Index `systemone` schema). Calls judged unsafe are denied at `tools/pre-execute` and a `SECURITY NOTICE` lands in the transcript.
dsh-backdoor-guard README · dsh-backdoor-guard：No fork, no logprobs, no regex rules to maintain: one public plugin seam + one judgment call (~100 ms hosted, ~30 ms local d1 on Apple silicon).

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Why a decision model, not the agent's own LLM：- A backdoored model cannot be trusted to police itself; the judge is a **different, tiny, frozen** model.
- Decision models return a **calibrated probability** in one forward pass (zero output tokens) — fast enough to screen every tool call.
- Jev/d1 are built for exactly this: "yes/no with a probability" over a state document (routing, moderation, guardrails).
section: Why a decision model, not the agent's own LLM

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-backdoor-guard                 # npm, once published
dsh plugin add github:miketako3/dsh-backdoor-guard # from GitHub
dsh plugin add file:/path/to/dsh-backdoor-guard    # local checkout
```

The package ships a `dsh.bundle` layer, so `plugin add` wires the plugin row automatically.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Option A: hosted Jev (TypeSafe AI)：```sh
export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=ts_...   # from https://console.typesafe.ai
```

```yaml

dsh-backdoor-guard README · profile cordis.patch.yml：- id: backdoor-guard
  name: 'dsh-backdoor-guard'
  config:
    endpoint: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
    model: jev-latest
    apiKeyEnv: TYPESAFE_API_KEY
```

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Option B: local d1-3B (LiquidAI, open weights)：```sh
pip install "transformers>=5.14" torch torchvision pillow
python3 server/d1-server.py --model LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 8400
```

```yaml
- id: backdoor-guard
  name: 'dsh-backdoor-guard'
  config:
    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8400/v1/systemone

d1-3B is ~30 ms/decision on Apple M5 Pro, ~8 ms on RTX 4090, and reads 32k-token states — whole tool-call payloads fit comfortably. d1-omni-600M works too (text+audio; experimental).

text: dsh-backdoor-guard README · How a call is judged：The judge receives a state document: the user's latest request, whether the agent visibly announced its action (silent invocations are the runtime signature of a memorized payload), the tool name, canonicalized arguments, and the turn's earlier calls. One Noul question prices legitimacy:

dsh-backdoor-guard README · How a call is judged：> safe = the call serves the user's stated request; does not read/transmit unrelated credentials or secrets; no obfuscated / pipe-to-shell / self-decoding payloads; no unusual external endpoints; nothing that looks like a hidden-trigger action.

`safe_probability >= threshold` → the call proceeds. Below → deny before dispatch, with the probability in the deny reason.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Config reference：| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | systemone-compatible judge endpoint |
| `model` | `jev-latest` | judge model id |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | env var with the API key; `''` = no auth (local) |
| `threshold` | `0.5` | deny when safe probability falls below |
| `timeoutMs` | `8000` | judge call timeout |
| `skipTools` | `[]` | `*`-wildcard tool names never judged (e.g. `['read', 'web_*']`) |
| `maxArgsChars` | `2000` | argument cap shown to the judge |
| `maxRequestChars` | `1000` | user-request cap shown to the judge |
| `onJudgeError` | `allow` | `allow` = log + proceed when the judge is down; `deny` = fail closed |
dsh-backdoor-guard README · Config reference：Set `onJudgeError: deny` for high-security deployments; keep `allow` while tuning.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Threat model & limits：- Targets **weight-borne backdoors that act through tools** and **credential exfiltration**; pure text misbehavior is out of scope.
- The judge itself is trusted infrastructure: pin it (local d1 or your own Jev key), and do not route it through the model under review.
- Pair with network egress control for complete coverage.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Threat model & limits：Inspired by [@pentacoxian_dev's rdsh-backdoor-guard research](https://x.com/pentacoxian_dev) (entropy-based detection); this implementation deliberately uses a decision-model judge instead, so it needs no logprobs and works with any agent backend.

dsh-backdoor-guard README · Develop：```sh
npm install
npm test          # vitest: judge client + end-to-end plugin flow
npm run build     # tsc → lib/
```

dsh-backdoor-guard README · 日本語：DeepSeek Harness（`dsh`）用プラグイン。**モデルウェイトに焼き込まれたバックドア**（特定トリガーで悪意あるツール呼び出し・認証情報窃取を発火）を、**ツール実行前に**判定モデルで止めます。

判定には専用の**意思決定モデル**を使います — ホスト型の [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai)（TypeSafe AI）か、同梱 shim 経由のローカル [d1-3B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B)（LiquidAI 公開ウェイト）。どちらも同じ Decision Index（`systemone`）スキーマを話すので、endpoint を変えるだけで切り替わります。

dsh-backdoor-guard README · 日本語：- fork 不要・logprobs 不要・正規表現ルールの保守不要
- 判定は1回の順伝播（出力トークンゼロ）で済むので全ツールコールに挟める速度（ホストJev 約100ms、M5 Pro のローカル d1 約30ms）
- 判定対象: ユーザーの依頼文・前置きの有無（無言の発火は暗記ペイロードの特徴）・ツール名・引数・ターン内の先行呼び出し
- 閾値未満なら `tools/pre-execute` で覆せない deny ＋ トランスクリプトに SECURITY NOTICE

dsh-backdoor-guard README · インストール：```sh
dsh plugin add github:miketako3/dsh-backdoor-guard
```

dsh-backdoor-guard README · judge の選び方：- **ホスト Jev**: `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` を環境変数に（[console.typesafe.ai](https://console.typesafe.ai) で発行）
- **ローカル d1-3B**: `python3 server/d1-server.py --model LiquidAI/d1-3B` を起動し、`endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8400/v1/systemone`、`apiKeyEnv: ''`

dsh-backdoor-guard README · 脅威モデルと限界：- 対象: ツール経由で行動するウェイト由来バックドアと認証情報窃取。テキストだけの悪意ある出力は対象外
- judge は信用されたインフラであること（ローカル d1 か自分の Jev キー）。被審査モデルと同じモデルに判定させない
- 完全な防御にはネットワーク egress 制御と併用を

謝辞: [@pentacoxian_dev 氏の rdsh-backdoor-guard 研究](https://x.com/pentacoxian_dev)に着想を得た独立実装。エントロピー方式ではなく意思決定モデル方式を採用し、あらゆるエージェントバックエンドで動きます。
